paragraphs: Friend, here's what this psalm teaches me: remember what God has done, and then ask Him for more. The sons of Korah start by saying the LORD restored Jacob and that "You forgave the iniquity of Your people; You covered all their sin." (Psalm 85:1-2) Only after that do they get bold and ask, "Will You not revive us again, that Your people may rejoice in You?" (Psalm 85:6) Remembering what He has done gives you something solid to stand on when you ask.

Then comes my favorite turn. After all that asking, the singer says, "I will listen to what God the LORD will say; for He will surely speak peace to His people and His saints." (Psalm 85:8) So prayer isn't only a baker talking at God. It's also a baker getting quiet, and I'm LOUD, so I'm preaching to myself right now. The singer is sure God will speak, and he trusts that what he hears will be good.

And that trust has a picture behind it. "Loving devotion and faithfulness have joined together; righteousness and peace have kissed." (Psalm 85:10) Those good things aren't fighting each other in God's plan. They belong together, and "righteousness will go before Him to prepare the way for His steps." (Psalm 85:13) So when you feel dried out, friend, do what this song does: remember, ask, then listen.
